dedupe_keys.name: hydrometric monitoring network of the icelandic meteorological office vatnshæðarmælakerfið

description: The Icelandic Meteorological Office runs the national hydrometric network of nearly 200 stations to gather basic information on the hydrology of Iceland. Most stations measure discharge, others measure water level or groundwater level, and some also measure other environmental variables; almost all have digital loggers with pressure sensors for water level, conductivity and temperature, run on solar power, and most report to the Met Office control centre at least once a day, with alarms to the duty phone when conductivity or water level passes set thresholds. Most of the network is run for the ministry of industry and the National Energy Authority, with agreements with the largest energy companies, the Road Administration, Reykjavík city bodies and others, and organised water level measurements go back to about 1900. Data from the stations can be viewed through the Met Office data server, and a 2012 map of the stations is available as a PDF. Access is free to view. Caveats: the data comes from an automatic system, is not quality checked, and the Met Office takes no responsibility for its use. Coverage is Iceland. It supports hazard exposure and early warning for glacial outburst floods and river floods affecting roads, bridges and hydropower; related records are the INAMHI hydrometeorological data and the CEMADEN observation network map.
